plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks crowned with huge golden flower heads that follow the sun across the sky. In midsummer fields, whole hillsides glow with their warm, radiant faces, buzzing with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early autumn (roughly July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Fields and gardens across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, including the central United States and southern and central Europe
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower but hundreds of tiny florets, and the seeds are packed in a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of fragrant purple blooms that hum with pollinators. The air around a lavender field in summer is sweet, herbal and calming.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to August in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Provence in southern France, and gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small Australian tree that erupts into fluffy golden pom-poms, lighting up the bush in late winter. Its honey-scented blossoms are a welcome sign that spring is coming.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (roughly July to September) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on 1 September.
